summary: Results/analysis review of notes/sim10_trace_20261110 at 3b1e9b3ac. Every numeric claim in README.md was reconciled against native/analysis-summary.json, complete.json, slurm.txt, the two timing phases JSON files and timeline-analysis.json: clean 15.1488/24.8319 s and 2.0646/1.2595 GiB/s; host-timed 16.3067/26.6205 s (7.64%/7.20% overhead); input.poll 0.6404/9.2928 (+8.6523), input.issue self 1.1665/2.7888 (+1.6223), read.wait -0.4235, read.pread_loop +0.0360, read.group -0.0978, task.callback -0.0453; the two increases sum to 10.2746 s = 99.6% of the 10.3138 s host-timed increase; clean increase 9.6831 s; explicit BD sync phases 0.00206/0.00207 s; cuStreamSynchronize 1.911/1.758 s; poll calls 50,101, visits 12,524,500/37,323,500 (+24,799,000), max 500/1000; Nsight loop 16.909/28.028 s vs receipts 35.35/45.53 s; kernel union 7.05/7.14 ms; GPU union 1.552/1.464 s; 100 of each kernel, stream 13 only vs 50/50 on 13/14; batch 20/21 intervals, durations, 501 polls, poll ms, copy union and following walk_xtc coordinates all match. Exclusive phases for two streams sum to 26.620347 s vs bd.loop total 26.620348 s and receipt 26.620505 s; startup+steady self_ns reproduce the whole-loop exclusive values. Poll counter arithmetic matches the mechanism: one stream 100 x (0+...+499) + 99 x 500 reclaimed-at-plan visits = 12,524,500; two streams additionally carry 500 retained windows across all 501 polls per batch plus 98 x 500 two-batch-old reclaims = 37,323,500, with reclaimed 49,500/49,000 as recorded. Frozen gpu_input_group.py, gpu_input_window.py and gpu_events.py are textually identical to psana/psana/gpu at this checkout; the cited code paths (plan_slots->poll, issue->poll, any(g.slot==slot) scan, poll skipping window-less groups, InputWindow._try_retire lock/state check returning False on live uses, never synchronizing) exist as described. analyze_trace.py SQL and union/clip math are correct for the claims made; it opens SQLite read-only and asserts one bd.loop and 100 group.issue ranges. Caveats in the README (timed-pair attribution, untimed slot scan, worker-thread sync separate, profiler elapsed outside bd.loop, traced-activity union, local-cache-cold only, single matched pair, no fix measured) are present and accurate; the proposed fix preserves ownership/credit/deferred retirement/error cleanup. Prior T1-T4 are closed or deferred nonblocking per responses.md and remain consistent with native evidence. Four new low, nonblocking documentation-precision findings.

findings.evidence: The 99.6% figure is a net attribution. Phases outside the table move by comparable magnitudes and cancel: allocation.owned_empty +0.238 s (1017 vs 511 startup allocations), group.submit +0.214 s, retire.consumer_join +0.164 s, pool.submit +0.063 s, versus read.wait -0.423 s, admission.plan -0.073 s, read.group -0.098 s. All other phases net to about +0.039 s.
findings.requested_change: Add one sentence stating that the remaining phases net to roughly +0.04 s but include offsetting changes of up to a few tenths of a second, so 99.6% should be read as a net share, not as the only phases that changed.

findings.evidence: The cuStreamSynchronize 1.91/1.76 s sum is attributed to KvikIO worker threads, but analyze_trace.py's cuda_api_summary groups by nameId only with no globalTid filter, and timeline-analysis.json itself lists 'CUDA API sums include multiple host threads' as a limitation. The thread attribution is inferred from the 50,000 call count matching the 50,000 read requests.
findings.requested_change: Either state that the worker-thread attribution is inferred from the per-read call count, or extend analyze_trace.py to group cuStreamSynchronize by globalTid and exclude the BD thread's tid before re-running on the exports.

findings.evidence: 'Repeated polling visits those windows even when live references make them ineligible' and 'Each such visit enters InputWindow._try_retire, takes its lock, and checks state' are source inferences. The visited_states counter records len(pool._groups) per poll, which includes window-less groups and does not count _try_retire entries or distinguish the live-use early return (line 127) from the event.done branch (line 136). The supporting measured evidence is that cudaEventQuery_v3020 stays at 150,000 calls in both captures, so no extra event queries were added by two streams.
findings.requested_change: Mark these two sentences as code-path inference and cite the equal cudaEventQuery counts (150,000 in both traces) as the measurement that rules out extra CUDA event queries; optionally note that visited_states counts all pool entries, not _try_retire entries.
